title: Conditions and Decision Making
subtitle: Make programs respond differently depending on conditions.
description: Learn if, else if, else and switch statements to create intelligent decision-making logic.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Conditions and Decision Making

Welcome to Lesson 4: Conditions and Decision Making. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Conditions and Decision Making”. The goal is to make programs respond differently depending on conditions.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.
A conditional statement lets a program select a path based on a Boolean expression. Put the most important conditions in a readable order and make the fallback behavior explicit.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select JavaScript. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.title: Sample 1: Conditions and Decision Making in practice

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Make programs respond differently depending on conditions. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: A form accepts an empty username even though one is required. What should the program do?
options: Treat the empty value as a valid username.
Change the button color only.
Save it and hope the database fixes it.
Check for empty or whitespace-only input and give a clear message.
blocks.explanation: Validation must check the actual input state and tell the user how to correct it.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Validation must check the actual input state and tell the user how to correct it.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Validation must check the actual input state and tell the user how to correct it.

blocks.text: PAGE 2 — Build the idea step by step

blocks.title: Sample 2: Conditions and Decision Making in practice

blocks.text: Application tip: in a real JavaScript project, choose names and structures that reveal the reason the code exists. Do not copy a snippet into a project without checking its assumptions and adapting it to the surrounding code.

blocks.question: A fallback branch never runs during testing. What should the developer verify?
options: The page has a newer color palette.
The earlier conditions do not already match every possible case.
The variable was renamed to a longer word.
The program has more comments.
blocks.explanation: An overly broad earlier condition can make a fallback unreachable.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. An overly broad earlier condition can make a fallback unreachable.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. An overly broad earlier condition can make a fallback unreachable.

blocks.text: Boundary values reveal many bugs. If a reward starts at 100 points, test 99, 100, and 101; testing only a typical value can hide an incorrect comparison operator.

blocks.code:

if (email.includes("@")) console.log("Check the full format too");

blocks.question: A reward begins at exactly 100 points, but the code awards it only when score is greater than 100. Which test exposes the bug?
options: Test only a score of 200.
Test a text value such as “high”.
Do not test the condition.
blocks.explanation: Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.

blocks.title: Sample 4: Conditions and Decision Making in practice

blocks.text: Before continuing, explain in your own words how this topic helps solve the dashboard goal: Learn if, else if, else and switch statements to create intelligent decision-making logic. Try one boundary case, one normal case, and one case that should be rejected or handled differently.

blocks.question: Two validation rules must both pass before submission. Which logical structure is appropriate?
options: Use OR if either rule must pass.
Skip validation once the page looks correct.
Combine both checks with the appropriate AND condition.
Run the same check forever.
blocks.explanation: AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.

blocks.question: A program has overlapping score bands. Which approach prevents a higher score from being assigned to a lower band?
options: Check bands in a clear order from higher threshold to lower threshold, or use non-overlapping ranges.
Use unrelated variable names.
Remove the boundary checks.
Make every branch print the same label.
blocks.explanation: Branch ordering and non-overlapping ranges avoid an earlier broad condition swallowing a later one.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Branch ordering and non-overlapping ranges avoid an earlier broad condition swallowing a later one.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Branch ordering and non-overlapping ranges avoid an earlier broad condition swallowing a later one.
